text.p: Swiss shares prices rose late in the day to end higher, supported by a better Wall Street opening and short covering, dealers said.
U.S. employement data, which was better than expected, did not have much effect, although the data did not soften interest rate fears, one trader noted. Trade was generally quiet.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index added 10.7 points, or 0.3 percent, to end at 3,637.8 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index rose 6.80 points, or 0.29 percent, to 2,332.70.
Roche certificates, which led the actives list, were unchanged at 8,975 francs.

UBS was a conspicuous winner among banks. UBS bearer shares rose 14 francs or 1.2 percent to 1,167. Dealers attributed the rise to a number of factors, such as a favourable Zurich court verdict for UBS in its quarrel with dissident shareholder BK Vision, to short covering and to technical factors.

Also, the shares may have been supported by strong gains in Swiss energy shares, one dealer said. Utility firm Motor Columbus, majority-owned by UBS, jumped three percent to 2,585. Elektrowatt, in which CS Holding has a stake, also firmed.
In the past, markets have speculated that Elektrowatt and Motor-Columbus could be combined in a Swiss energy holding.
CS Holding was down one franc to 122.
Food group Nestle was up nine francs to 1,402 and pharmaceuticals Ciba and Sandoz gained around 0.6 percent each.
Insurers were mixed. Swiss Re lost three francs to close at 1,294.
